newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke "not persuaded" rates need rise.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke "not persuaded" rates need rise.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Monday he was not convinced interest rates need to rise. Clarke told BBC Radio there was no sign of consumer demand accelerating. He said factory gate prices remained subdued and the strong pound "was having an effect."
"I am not so far persuaded interest rates need to go up," he said.

Clarke said it had become fashionable in recent months for economic pundits to demand tax and interest rate rises but he argued that the British economy was growing at a sustainable rate -- "a Goldilocks recovery" he called it.
